Two Ferrari F40 "Abandoned" on Google Maps: A YouTuber's Disillusioning Hunt

2026-10-03 Auto Plus Google Maps, Ferrari F40, Pontiac Fiero, replica, kit car, satellite imagery, YouTuber, Spain, supercar, automotive discovery
Read the source article

Quick summary

French automotive outlet Auto Plus recounts how a Spanish YouTuber spotted what appeared to be two abandoned Ferrari F40s on Google Maps in rural Spain, only to discover on-site that both were cheap replicas built on Pontiac Fiero chassis — illustrating how satellite imagery can deceive.

Key takeaways

  • A Spanish YouTuber identified two apparent Ferrari F40s abandoned in rural Spain using Google Maps satellite imagery
  • The first "F40" was found in a barn near the Portuguese border, surrounded by old cars, but turned out to be a replica built on a Pontiac Fiero chassis
  • The second "F40" near Valencia was also a Pontiac Fiero-based replica; the owner offered to sell it for $35,000 (approximately €32,000)
  • The Pontiac Fiero is the preferred base for Ferrari F40 replicas due to its mid-engine layout, appropriate size, affordability, and availability
  • The story highlights how Google Maps satellite imagery can create misleading impressions of automotive discoveries, with reality often far less glamorous
